short: Henry VIII disbanded Catholic monasteries, priories, and convents across England and Wales.
full:
Beginning in 1536, chief minister Thomas Cromwell orchestrated the systematic suppression of religious houses in England and Wales on behalf of Henry VIII. The ruthless campaign started with the statutory dissolution of smaller, impoverished monasteries and escalated systematically until the surrender of Waltham Abbey on 23 March 1540, successfully liquidating over eight hundred religious institutions that had existed for centuries.

The dissolution fundamentally transferred a staggering portion of the nation's wealth, land, and resources from the Church directly to the Crown and its favoured nobles. It destroyed the infrastructure of English monasticism, abruptly removed a primary societal source of charity, medicine, and education, and bound the landed gentry financially to the survival of the Reformation.
